questions.q: What problem does partitioning a fact table solve that a clustered columnstore index alone does not?
options: Fast, low-overhead loading of new data and purging of old data, instead of row-by-row operations against the whole table
It makes the table return incorrect query results faster
It removes the need for any indexes on the table at all
It automatically deletes duplicate rows
questions.explain: A columnstore index speeds up querying, but loading and purging large chunks of data against one undivided table structure is still slow — partitioning addresses that operational problem.

questions.q: What does a CREATE PARTITION FUNCTION statement actually define?
options: How column values map to partition numbers, based on boundary values
Which filegroups the partitions live on
The clustered index for the table
The foreign key relationships for the table
questions.explain: The partition function defines the boundaries that map a column's values to partition numbers; the partition scheme then maps those partition numbers to filegroups.

questions.q: Why is a fact table's date key almost always chosen as the partitioning column?
options: Date is the natural boundary for both loading new data and purging old data on a retention window
SQL Server only allows partitioning on date columns
Date columns are always the primary key of a fact table
Partition functions cannot be defined on integer columns
questions.explain: Loading (new day's/month's data) and purging (data older than a retention window) both naturally align with date boundaries, which is why the date key is the typical partitioning column.

questions.q: Given CREATE PARTITION FUNCTION PF (INT) AS RANGE RIGHT FOR VALUES (20220101, 20230101, 20240101, 20250101), how many partitions does this create?
options: Five: before 2022, one per year through 2024, and 2025 onward
Four, one for each boundary value listed
One single partition containing all the data
Zero — this syntax is invalid
questions.explain: A RANGE partition function creates n + 1 partitions for n boundary values — here, 4 boundary values produce 5 partitions.

questions.q: What does ALTER TABLE ... SWITCH PARTITION do, and why does it matter operationally?
options: It moves an entire partition in or out of a table as a fast metadata operation, regardless of row count, instead of a slow row-by-row copy or delete
It permanently deletes the partitioned table
It converts a rowstore table to columnstore
It renames a partition function
questions.explain: SWITCH is what makes partitioning operationally valuable: a load can switch a new partition in, and a retention job can switch the oldest partition out, both near-instantly.
